name: Bounded Solo-Maintainer Release
summary: Execute an explicitly owner-authorised release under a narrow recorded solo-maintainer exception while preserving exact-head checks, protected merge, rollback and runtime evidence.
problem: A sole maintainer can be blocked by a non-author review rule, while informal workarounds risk inventing approval or silently weakening release and target-system boundaries.
coreOutcomes: Explicit owner authority and a bounded policy exception
Technical review distinguished from independent approval and formal scanning
Exact candidate, merged tree and deployed revision reconciliation
Normal protected merge with stale-head rejection
Rollback preparation, smoke tests and independent runtime readback
Provider scan clearance separated from live-case and publication acceptance
requirements: Explicit owner-authorised exception for an owner-controlled release
Current repository governance and required checks
Exact candidate source and immutable validation evidence
Existing authorised merge and deployment mechanisms
Read-only production and provider acceptance surfaces
boundaries: Reviewer absence does not automatically authorise an exception
Does not impersonate reviewers or grant authority over inspected systems
Does not disable protections or waive unrelated checks
Manual technical review is not a formal security scan
Deployment and scanner success do not establish publication or customer adoption
